data.name: Jagannath
data.gender_notes: Jagannath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jagannath refers to Lord Krishna or Lord Vishnu, the supreme ruler and controller of the universe. This powerful name signifies protection, strength, and the ultimate authority. The name Jagannath carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jagannath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jagannath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jagannath total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Ganesha is a widely worshipped deity and is recognized as the remover of obstacles and the god of new beginnings in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Ganesha symbolizes the power of the individual will and helps in removing obstacles on the spiritual path.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jagannath means 'Lord of the Universe'. He is the embodiment of Vishnu, the preserver in the Hindu Trimurti. Worship of Jagannath signifies surrendering to the divine power that governs the universe.

vedic_reference.note: Jagannath is the presiding deity of the Puri Jagannath Temple, one of the most famous and ancient temples in India. He is an avatar of Lord Vishnu and is worshipped as the Lord of the Universe.

historical_references.reference: Jagannath Temple at Puri is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites in India. The temple is believed to have been built by King Indradyumna in the 11th or 12th century CE.

Another tradition states that Jagannath was the name of a deity worshipped by the Gangas of Odisha in the 13th century CE. According to this tradition, King Anangabhima III of the Ganga dynasty had installed the present idols of Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra in the temple in 1264 CE.
historical_references.context: Installation of Jagannath idols in Puri

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Jagannath continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Jagannath, a teacher in Delhi, India, shares that their name Jagannath meaning "Lord of the Universe" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
